zurand

zurand is a random number generator for R in which every value is a pure function of a key and its position, so drawing never reads or changes .Random.seed.

  • A key gives the same values on Linux, macOS and Windows, on x86_64 and ARM, and at any thread count.
  • Drawing more values, or drawing in another order, leaves every other result unchanged, so parallel tasks need no seeds.
  • On one thread it is 8 to 17 times faster than runif() and rnorm(), and large draws use several threads without changing a value.

It builds on the counter-based generators of Random123 and on xoshiro256++.

Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

install.packages("zurand")

Or the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zurand")

Usage

A key gives the same numbers every time you use it, and asking for more extends the sequence rather than changing it:

library(zurand)

key <- rng_key(2026)
rng_normal(key, 3)
#> [1]  0.006686381 -1.233412249  0.591067060
rng_normal(key, 5)
#> [1]  0.006686381 -1.233412249  0.591067060  0.835300390  0.249764157

For several independent streams, such as the replicates of a simulation, make a vector of keys. Each column is the stream of one key:

keys <- rng_key(2026, n = 3)
rng_normal(keys, 4)
#>              [,1]       [,2]        [,3]
#> [1,]  0.006686381 -2.2711494  0.42616283
#> [2,] -1.233412249 -0.2468333  0.05688975
#> [3,]  0.591067060  0.9256739 -1.02992948
#> [4,]  0.835300390  1.1623784  0.68884687

zurand also draws uniform values and integers, derives keys from names, and makes lazy vectors of any length; Get started shows how.
